system.summary: The compared sign ciphers use distinct alphabets, mostly one invented sign per Arabic letter with a dotted-stem word divider, some with a second shape for a letter, a tashifi alphabet of one sign per undotted letter shape, a letter-reordering (maqlub) text in ordinary letters, and a tree script whose branch counts give the letter's abjad word and its place in it.

diacritics.note: Dots are not enciphered; in the tashifi run (14v.7) one sign stands for all the letters of one undotted shape.

system.sibling_key: none: no two ciphers compared share an alphabet (keys_eye/REPORT.md); 20r.8 and 47r.1, and 46v.11 and 13r.1, are each one cipher split by the misbound quire 3
system.notes: A few ciphers write one letter with two shapes (for example lam in 31r.2 and 13r.11, sad in 63v.1, dal in 18r.11); most have one shape per letter. The by-eye keys show signs often made from the plain letter's own shape (a ta-like sign for ta, teeth for sin), but different letters for the same shape in different ciphers. Lam-alif is one sign in some ciphers (the compiler says so, 22r). The tree script (63v) follows the qalam mushajjar rule of Ibn al-Durayhim's Miftah al-kunuz (Mrayati et al., vol. 1, 1987, p. 335). distinct_symbols differs per cipher (11 to 32 shapes in the keyed chains).

prior_solution.where: The compiler's own decipherments are on the page after (almost) every cipher, and some ciphers carry a red letter over each sign; they are contemporary. No modern study, edition or decipherment of LJS 51 was found (research/ljs51_pass/prior_art.md, prior_art_2.md: Penn, Schoenberg, Digital Scriptorium, Mrayati et al. vols. 1-2, Mir 'Alam 2018, Qalqashandi, DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry, web searches). The tree-script rule is printed in Ibn al-Durayhim's Miftah al-kunuz (Mrayati et al., vol. 1, Damascus 1987, p. 335), found after the 63v decoding.

solution.what: Page pass: 212 page images (OPenn web JPEGs, 1422 px) read by agents; 209 cipher chains listed with their plaintexts, 28 apparent gaps re-checked, DECODE (10,106 record summaries) and a prior-art search (research/ljs51_pass/).
All 212 OPenn master TIFFs (2339 x 2959 px) fetched by curl for the master transcription.
Segmenter v1 (segment.py): line finder and sign cutter scored against by-eye counts (evaluate.py); 90% of reference lines within one sign.
Rekey pilot (rekey.py, pilot_report.md) on three chains: the tashifi key rebuilt from scratch by DP alignment with the compiler's plaintext; short chains gave too little for an automatic key.
Tashifi run 14v.7 vetted (research/ljs51_pass/vet_tashifi.md): 15 sign classes for the 15 undotted letter shapes, as the compiler describes; 722 of 756 aligned signs in their class.

Chain records from the master TIFFs, images 6-217 (chains_*.jsonl, chains_all.json): sign counts per line by eye, sign inventory, red gloss, the compiler's technique notes and his plaintext read word by word.
English translation of every plaintext (eight translation_*.md files), each ending with a list of suspected Arabic errors.
Restricted automatic rebuild (keys_fork/): control reproduced, 6v.11 in part, 20r.8 at chance against the 21r prose; 62 chains skipped for segmentation.
Errata: 131 suspected errors of the records checked on the masters (errata.md): 32 misreadings, 56 the page's own forms, 43 not settled; the misreadings applied (fixes_log.jsonl).

Recheck of the unanswered chains (chains_missed.jsonl, recheck_unanswered.jsonl): 46v.11 continues on 13r (one cipher of the verses 13r l.5-7); 49r.1 answered by the last 12 words of the 49r verses; 48r.8 answered by the 21r prose (group-length search, 43 of 49 groups); 12v.8 and 12v.11 lose their 13r candidates.
30v.7: a group-length search over all 1,034 passages of the book for its 20 groups (best 9 of 20 lengths right) and a reading of ff. 30r-31v.

By-eye keys (keys_eye/): each cipher's signs labelled on line crops of the master and aligned word by word with the compiler's plaintext; key table, consistency over repeated shapes, red-gloss agreement; the key built on the text as enciphered where it differs from the written copy.
Red glosses read sign by sign on the masters and compared with the by-eye keys (keys_eye/REPORT.md, red_check fields).

f. 63v tree script: tested abjad numeral value (19/79 trees), alphabetical grids (10-28/79); then right-side branches = abjad word, left-side branches = place in the word: 78 of 79 trees (3.15 under a tear). The sign cipher 63v.1 and the trees independently correct four words of the record's plaintext.

Prior art, second pass (prior_art_2.md): Mrayati et al. vols. 1-2 (the Miftah's tree-script rule, vol. 1 p. 335; al-maqlub and al-ibdal its first two kinds), Mir 'Alam 2018, Qalqashandi, Shawq al-mustaham; no mention of LJS 51 or its decipherments.

Identification of the compiler checked against Safadi, Ibn Hajar and Mrayati (identity_ibn_durayhim.md) and re-read on the masters (identity_readings.md): 102v 'my book Miftah al-kunuz fi hall al-marmuz', 50r the laqab al-Durayhim of his ancestor, 49r 'I have written works on it', 62r after the death of the patron's brother; identification strongly supported, the compiler never names himself.

Codicology: quire 3 (ff. 13-20) is bound out of place and belongs between ff. 46 and 47 (46v->13r split inside a word; 20r-20v is the first half of the 47r riddle cipher); 21r l.1-5 is the end of the 48r.8 cipher. Penn's collation of q6-q7 needs a physical check.
Another session annealed 48r.8 blind (ar-mamluk) and reached the 21r riddle; that cipher is written up on its own page (ljs51f48r).
3v.12 tested against its plaintext as a simple substitution: best 25 of 42 signs, chance level; key not recovered, the piece stays answered in part.
